what: Remove Duplicate Lines cleans a list by deleting every line that appears more than once, keeping only the first copy in its original place. It can also ignore differences in capital letters, trim stray spaces, drop empty lines and sort the result from A to Z.

It is useful for anyone who works with lists: email addresses for a newsletter, product codes, keywords, names from a sign-up sheet, URLs, or rows copied from a spreadsheet. Instead of checking hundreds of lines by eye, you get a clean, unique list in one click and a message telling you how many lines were removed.
Your list is processed in your browser, so it is never uploaded.
uses: Paste addresses collected from several forms and keep each address only once before importing them into your mail tool.
Combine keyword lists from different tools and remove the repeats.
Join sign-up lists from two events and get one list of unique people.
Copy a column from Excel or Google Sheets, remove duplicates here, and paste the clean column back.
Make sure each link, SKU or ID appears only once before you process it.
tutorial: Click the box "Your list (one item per line)" and paste your items, one on each line. You can copy a column straight from a spreadsheet; each cell becomes a line.
When ticked, "Apple", "APPLE" and "apple" count as the same line and only the first one is kept. It is off by default, so lines must match exactly.
This option is on by default. It removes spaces at the start and end of each line, so "apple " and "apple" count as the same. Turn it off only if leading spaces matter, for example in code.
"Remove empty lines" is on by default and deletes all blank lines. Untick it to keep the first blank line; later blank lines are still removed as duplicates.
Tick "Sort A to Z" to put the clean list in alphabetical order. The sort ignores capital letters and puts numbers in natural order, so item2 comes before item10.
The box is replaced with the clean list. A green message shows what happened, for example "Removed 38 of 250 lines. 212 left."
Click "Copy" and paste the list where you need it.
features: Duplicates are removed but the original order of first appearances stays the same.
Treat capital and small letters as the same when needed.
Ignores invisible spaces at the start and end of lines that often cause false differences.
Removes blank lines in the same step.
Optional sorting that handles numbers inside text sensibly.
Shows how many lines were removed and how many are left.

example.title: Worked example: cleaning a sign-up list
example.text: You paste 8 lines: "anna@mail.com", "Ben@mail.com", "anna@mail.com ", an empty line, "ben@mail.com", "cara@mail.com", "anna@mail.com" and "dan@mail.com". You tick "Ignore upper/lower case" and keep "Trim spaces" and "Remove empty lines" on. After you click "Remove duplicates", 4 lines are left: anna@mail.com, Ben@mail.com, cara@mail.com and dan@mail.com. The message says "Removed 4 of 8 lines. 4 left." The extra space after the second anna was trimmed, so it was found as a repeat.

tips: When the case option is on, the first spelling is the one that stays. Put the version you prefer first.
For email addresses, always tick "Ignore upper/lower case", because Anna@Mail.com and anna@mail.com reach the same inbox.
If you need a count of how many times each item appeared, note the numbers before removing them; this tool only keeps unique lines.
A list separated by commas must be put on separate lines first. The Notepad tool’s "Split lines at a character" can do that.
Keep a copy of the original list if you might need it, because the box is replaced with the result.
problems: Lines that look the same were not removed

They differ in a hidden way, such as a tab, two spaces between words, or a different but similar-looking character. Make sure "Trim spaces" is on, and tick "Ignore upper/lower case" if capitals differ.
My items are all on one line
The tool works line by line. Put each item on its own line, for example by replacing commas with line breaks.
The removed count is higher than I expected
Empty lines are also counted as removed when "Remove empty lines" is on.
"Sort A to Z" was ticked. Untick it, paste the original list again and run it once more to keep the first-seen order.
